correctness.rationale: Every cyclic order-m word has a unique \(0^m\) edge, so a complete non-repeating DFS through the de Bruijn graph lists each canonical linearization exactly once; 1,1,2,16,2048 words are obtained for \(m=1,\ldots,5\). For each completed word all nonempty substrings are tested directly for a border with exactly two overlapping-allowed occurrences, then checked for left/right maximality. A separate strict-record-LCP method produces precisely the same endpoint pairs for every word. Exact histograms and witness strings replay successfully from the standalone standard-library program; no extrapolation or solver claim is made.

value.rationale: The number of maximal closed substring occurrences is the output-dependent cost parameter of current enumeration algorithms. Binary de Bruijn cycles are standard maximally factor-diverse benchmarks, and order five has a complete, naturally bounded population of 2048 cycles (the next order has 67,108,864). The complete exact histogram, including eight minimizers at 40 and eight maximizers at 54, quantifies real 35% variation on inputs of identical length and window coverage; this is a nontrivial finite classification rather than a generic example or arbitrary slice.
